prompts.stack_overflow: Use case: stylized-concept. Production 16-bit pixel-art game sprite atlas. Match reference Linter Enforcer's dark navy outline weight, crisp chunky pixel clusters, slate steel, cyan and lime glow, restrained three-tone shading and belt-scroller three-quarter view. NEW mini-boss STACK OVERFLOW: a tottering tower of FIVE heavy rectangular call-stack terminal frames, cyan/lime horizontal slot glyphs (not words), slightly offset stacked steel slabs forming head and torso, small angry cyan eyes in top slab, thick segmented robotic arms, broad clenched block fists, two short mechanical legs with heavy boots. Tall top-heavy readable silhouette, comic menace. Exactly FOUR columns FOUR rows, 16 full-body complete isolated poses at consistent scale, face LEFT throughout, generous 30px outer margin and wide transparent gutters, no sprite touches another. Row-major cells: 1 idle stacked upright; 2 idle stack tilts slightly; 3 walk left foot forward; 4 walk passing; 5 walk right foot forward; 6 walk passing opposite; 7 slam warning arms rising; 8 slam warning arms overhead and stack stretches; 9 smash both fists DOWN toward left at floor; 10 slam followthrough crouched fists on floor; 11 dash warning crouched forward lean; 12 dash left charging boot stride A; 13 dash left stride B, stack trailing right; 14 recovery braced upright; 15 hurt recoils backward; 16 defeated low toppled heap of the SAME stack frames and limbs, nothing standing. One character per cell. TRUE TRANSPARENT alpha background, no floor/shadows, no labels, text, numbers, borders, UI, detached particles or floating effect rings. The source character should fill about 65% of each cell vertically so packing can make standing height 98px inside a 192px cell. Clean usable sprite sheet, not concept art.
